title: Integral surjective test-base replacement for arbitrary constant-ring coefficients
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $p:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and $q\in\mathbf Z$ with $q\geq1$. Assume $\mathrm{BC}(p,\Lambda,q-1)$ in the fixed-base, single-degree sense of [sk-def-bc]. Let $g:T\to S$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let $\pi:T'\to T$ be integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Form the Cartesian squares of $p$ along $g$ and $g'=g\circ\pi$, with projections $e:Y=X\times_ST\to T$, $h:Y\to X$, $e':Y'=X\times_ST'\to T'$ and $h':Y'\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and put $F'=\pi^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. If the canonical map
$$p^{-1}R^qg'_*F'\longrightarrow R^qh'_*e'^{-1}F'$$
is an isomorphism, then the canonical map
$$p^{-1}R^qg_*F\longrightarrow R^qh_*e^{-1}F$$
is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, sk-def-bc]. No integer annihilator or invertibility hypothesis on $\Lambda$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $G=\pi_*F'=\pi_*\pi^{-1}F$ and let $\eta:F\to G$ be the adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. The module adjunction has the underlying abelian unit by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](2),(3). For every $t'\in T'$ choose an algebraic closure of its residue field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and the corresponding geometric point $\bar t'$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and set $\bar t=\pi\bar t'$. These image geometric points cover $T$, by surjectivity [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. A germ of $G$ at $\bar t$ represented by $b\in G(U)=F'(U\times_TT')$ maps to the germ of $b$ at the pointed etale neighbourhood $(U\times_TT',(\bar u,\bar t'))$ of $\bar t'$. The section formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] makes this assignment compatible with every restriction, hence gives a homomorphism $r_{\bar t'}:G_{\bar t}\to F'_{\bar t'}$. The unit-germ identity of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] says $c_{\pi,\bar t',F}\,r_{\bar t'}\,\eta_{\bar t}=1_{F_{\bar t}}$, so each such $\eta_{\bar t}$ is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono] to the underlying abelian unit. It is mono, and so is the module unit: if two module maps have equal composites with it, their underlying abelian maps are equal, hence the module maps are equal. This uses no finite-stalk product formula.

source.place: Tag 0F04, lemma-base-change-q-integral-top, proof; arbitrary-Lambda form as in IntegralBaseChange.lean:125-160

proof.text: Write $b_M:p^{-1}R^qg_*M\to R^qh_*e^{-1}M$. Apply [lem-sbc-integral-test-pushforward-arrow] to the given integral $\pi$, with $M=F'$ and $r=q$. Its isomorphisms $A_{F'}$ and $B_{F'}$ satisfy $B_{F'}b_G=b'_{F'}A_{F'}$. The hypothesis says $b'_{F'}$ is an isomorphism; therefore $b_G=B_{F'}^{-1}b'_{F'}A_{F'}$ is an isomorphism. The cited statement identifies the arrows themselves, so no inference is being made from endpoint isomorphisms alone. Neither a torsion assumption nor an extension of the lower-degree hypothesis to other coefficient categories is used.

source.place: Tag 0F04, lemma-base-change-q-integral-top, proof; arbitrary-Lambda form as in IntegralBaseChange.lean:125-160

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-fixed-base-critical-map](1),(2) to the fixed morphism $p$, the given qcqs $g$, the integer $q\ge1$, and the module monomorphism $\eta:F\hookrightarrow G$ from Step 1. Its hypothesis is precisely $\mathrm{BC}(p,\Lambda,q-1)$ at the fixed base, which is assumed here. We obtain that $b_F$ is mono and that $\operatorname{Coker}(b_F)\to\operatorname{Coker}(b_G)$ is mono. The existing universally quantified injectivity node cannot be applied with only this fixed-base hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0F04, lemma-base-change-q-integral-top, proof; arbitrary-Lambda form as in IntegralBaseChange.lean:125-160

proof.text: Since $b_G$ is an isomorphism by Step 2, its cokernel is zero. The monomorphism from Step 3 embeds $\operatorname{Coker}(b_F)$ in zero, so this cokernel is zero as well. Thus $b_F$ is epi and mono, hence an isomorphism in the abelian category [def-sp-abelian] of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. This is the required canonical comparison map.

theorem Etale.isIso_baseChangeHomologyMap_of_isIntegralHom_of_surjective (q : ℤ) (hq : 1 ≤ q)
    (hprev : Etale.BaseChangeProperty Λ p (q - 1)) [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (sq : IsPullback e h g p) (π : T' ⟶ T) [IsIntegralHom π] (hπ : Function.Surjective π.base)
    (sq' : IsPullback e' h' (π ≫ g) p) (F : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hF : IsIso (Etale.baseChangeHomologyMap Λ sq' q ((π)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ].obj F))) :
    IsIso (Etale.baseChangeHomologyMap Λ sq q F)
lean.note: Exact source declaration: its fixed-base Etale.BaseChangeProperty hypothesis, q ≥ 1, qcqs g, integral and surjective π, Cartesian squares, module sheaf F and inverse-image pullback hypothesis, and canonical degree-q base-change isomorphism conclusion match this node.
